work.text: Attested GPU cards. A miner installs TargonOS, a signed operating system that wipes the machine and attests it to the network on every boot, and keeps confidential virtual machines available for rent. What is paid for is a live, verified card inside an auction class, whether or not a customer is using it. There is no request or response the miner answers.
work.quote: Miner emissions are paid per card based on each auction's target price and the amount of compute live on the network

scoring.text: No quality score. Each auction, fetched from the Tower service, names target cards, a target price and a cap in cents per card hour. The pool is target price times target cards; each verified card earns the lesser of pool divided by live cards and the cap, times 1.2, as a fraction of the dollar value of the miner emission pool, itself computed from chain emission and the TAO price.

split.text: Proportional to verified cards in each auction, capped per card. Weight no auction covers is burned: split among the burn keys Tower names, remainder to uid 28. If payouts exceed the pool, every weight scales down pro rata. A node reporting fewer cards than the auction's min_cluster_size, 8 for the H200 and B200 classes in the docs example, earns nothing from that auction.

judges.text: Seven validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot, against five miners. Commit-reveal is on, weights at most once per 100 blocks. A validator re-attests each miner node during the interval, counts its GPU cards against the auction's cluster minimum, prices it from Tower's auction table, and posts the weight extrinsic through a weights-api sidecar. Nothing about the compute's quality is judged, only its presence and attestation.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 7

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes, and the validator works in the same interval: it fetches auctions and the emission pool at the start, polls miner nodes every 30 blocks, and sets weights once per interval. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 7,520 blocks, about 25 hours, half again the usual 5,000.

buyer.text: Renters of confidential GPU and CPU machines by the hour, through the site and an unauthenticated inventory API. Prices run from $0.45 an hour for one RTX 4090 to $60 for an eight-card B300 class. On 2026-09-19 the inventory listed 33 SKUs, of which 7 showed any availability. No customer is named; the front page shows a logo strip and counters that read zero.

exploits.text: Free compute drew abuse. The May 2025 post says subsidised inference on other companies' models attracts a queue that leaves when prices rise, so emission will not fund it. The guard in code is attestation: only nodes that pass TargonOS attestation and report at least the cluster minimum enter an auction, and weight no auction covers burns rather than paying idle registrations.
exploits.quote: If we opened a gas station and cut our prices to $0, we would expect a line of cars
